newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures stable, NYMEX offers no direction.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures stable, NYMEX offers no direction.

text.p: IPE Brent futures were holding around mid-range on Friday afternoon with early NYMEX markets offering little direction, traders said.
Front-month Brent trading bobbed either side of mid-range on the NYMEX opening as NYMEX products came in firmer then dipped back from the highs with NYMEX crude showing similar tendencies.
At 1452 GMT May Brent was trading 19 cents up at $18.12 a barrel with the May/June spread standing at around $17 in contango.
May gas oil was steady at $164, up $3.50 on the day.

Brent gained in early trade on news of a Tehran-Bonn political row and cold U.S. weather. Technicals were also supportive although Brent and NYMEX crude were see creeping out of the oversold region, brokers said.
Brokers said reports that a new cold spell would affect the United States up to early next week also gave a boost to the market, especially May gas oil.
And Iran's diplomatic stand-off with the European Union put oil traders on alert on Friday amid some concern that an escalation might threaten vital oil supplies.

European oil companies including France's Total and Anglo-Dutch oil giant Shell said on Friday they would not be deterred from investments in Iran despite a new crisis in relations between the European Union and Tehran.
However, brokers said the market will be watching to see if the Germany-Iran row worsens.
Analysts said that while the dispute would have no immediate impact on oil supply from Iran, it could force the EU to drop its opposition to U.S. trade sanctions against Tehran.
